chunk_findings.detail: The fix shortens the *head* of the shown command from the previous 200 characters to `_CMD_SHOWN - _CMD_SHOWN // 3 - 3` = 131 characters, and drops the middle covering `[131, len(cmd)-66)`. For any holder command line longer than ~200 characters whose identifying token lands in that dropped window, the new message hides the exact thing the change claims to preserve, whereas the pre-fix code (which showed the first 200 characters) surfaced it. Concretely, take a holder whose `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` decodes to `python3 -c "<125 chars of inline preamble>from ddflow.infra.log import _flock …" <lock>` (no long interpreter path, so the pre-fix code was not even affected here). Old output: `pid N (python3 -c <preamble> … ddflow.infra.log …)` — the module name sits at offset ≈136, inside the old 200-char head. New output: `pid N (python3 -c <first 131 chars>...<last 66 chars>)`, and if the total length exceeds ~267 the module name at 136 is neither in `cmd[:131]` nor in `cmd[-66:]`, so it is gone. The same happens for a `python3 … <subcommand>` invocation where the identifying subcommand/`-m` target is pushed past offset 131 by long options. In other words, any input whose identifying token falls in `[131, min(199, len(cmd)-67))` is strictly worse than before the change: the previous `[:200]` head showed it, the new 131-char head + 66-char tail does not.

chunk_findings.detail: The commit's stated invariant — "A line still too long keeps its first _CMD_SHOWN characters and gains its tail, so nothing shown before is lost" — is false for the tail. Before the change, `tail = _CMD_SHOWN // 3` = 66, so the message ended with the last 66 characters; now it ends with `cmd[-_CMD_TAIL:]` = the last 60. Characters at offsets 61–66 from the end that were previously visible are now inside the elided middle. Concrete input: a holder cmdline whose basenamed form is 300 characters long and whose identifying argument sits 62 characters from the end (e.g. `... <56 chars> --hold dd` — old note contained it via `cmd[-66:]`, new note cuts it because `cmd[-60:]` starts 6 characters later); for the trivial case `cmd = "x"*300` the old note exposed `x` at offset −66..−61 and the new one does not. The test added in the same commit (`test_a_long_command_still_shows_everything_the_old_cut_showed`) only checks a token at offset ~150, i.e. in the head, so it does not protect the tail budget that was silently reduced.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py `_describe_pid` (truncation line, new `cmd = f"{cmd[:_CMD_SHOWN]}...{cmd[-_CMD_TAIL:]}"`)

chunk_findings.detail: Replacing `argv[0].startswith("python")` with `_PYTHON.fullmatch(argv[0])` no longer matches real CPython interpreter basenames that carry a `t`/`d` suffix. Free-threaded builds are installed as `python3.13t` (PEP 703) and debug builds as `python3.13d` / Debian's `python3-dbg`; all of these matched the old `startswith("python")` and fail `fullmatch(r"python[0-9.]*")`. For such a holder the script argument is no longer reduced to its basename, so a long script path is emitted verbatim and eats the `_CMD_SHOWN` head — the exact failure mode this bug is about. Concrete input: `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` = `b"/usr/bin/python3.13t\0/very/long/scratch/path/to/entrypoint.py\0-m\0ddflow.infra.log\0"`; the new code returns `pid <n> (python3.13t /very/long/scratch/path/to/entrypoint.py -m ddflow.infra.log)` (and with a longer path the `ddflow.infra.log` argument is pushed past the 200-char head), whereas the old code produced `python3.13t entrypoint.py ...`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log.py `_PYTHON = re.compile(r"python[0-9.]*")`

chunk_findings.detail: Given `cmd` of length 266 with an identifying 6-character token at indices 200..205 (reachable when a holder's argv yields, e.g., `python3 -m ddflow <args> lock-1 ...` sized to 266), the old code rendered `cmd[:131] + "..." + cmd[-66:]`, whose tail started at index 200 and therefore printed that token. The new code renders `cmd[:200] + "..." + cmd[-60:]`; the head stops at index 199 and the tail starts at index 206, so indices 200..205 — content the previous implementation displayed — are silently dropped. This contradicts the new docstring's "nothing shown before is lost" and the new test's name (`test_a_long_command_still_shows_everything_the_old_cut_showed`), which never exercises a token that lives between the new head end (199) and the new tail start (206). The test passes only because it places its marker at offset 152 and its tail marker inside the final 60 characters.

chunk_findings.detail: The new pattern `python[0-9.]*[a-z]?(-dbg)?` only ever accepts **one** trailing ABI-suffix letter, but CPython's ABI flags compose: a build configured with both free-threading (`--disable-gil`, suffix `t`) and `--with-pydebug` (suffix `d`) installs its interpreter as `python3.13td` (or `python3.13dt`, depending on flag ordering). `_PYTHON.fullmatch("python3.13td")` returns `None`: `[0-9.]*` consumes `3.13`, `[a-z]?` consumes one letter, and the second suffix letter is left over (the `(-dbg)?` group cannot absorb it). Since `_describe_pid` only takes the "names its script" branch for a recognized interpreter, such a process falls into the fallback that shows the raw argv, so for a cmdline like `/long/scratch/.../venv/bin/python3.13td\0-m\0ddflow.infra.log\0...` the 200-char head (`_CMD_SHOWN`) is still entirely the long interpreter path and the identifying `ddflow.infra.log` part is still cut off — i.e. bug B3a4bf051b4 reproduces verbatim on exactly the "build-suffixed interpreter" class this hunk claims to fix. The added regression test cannot catch this because it only parametrizes the single-suffix names `python3.13t`, `python3.13d`, `python3-dbg`, `python`, and uses a short `/usr/bin/...` path.
